name: Ladakh
summary: High passes, blue lakes and quiet monasteries on the roof of India.
description: Ladakh is a cold desert between the Karakoram and the Great Himalaya. Roads climb over 5,000 m passes, valleys open into sand dunes, and lakes change colour through the day. It is the classic Indian motorcycle trip, and just as good from a car window.
highlights: Khardung La and Chang La passes

faqs.question: Do I need a permit?
faqs.answer: Indian citizens need an Inner Line Permit for Nubra, Pangong and other protected areas. We arrange it; you only send your ID in advance.

faqs.question: How do I deal with the altitude?
faqs.answer: Every Ladakh tour starts with rest days in Leh. Drink plenty of water, skip alcohol for the first days and tell your coordinator early if you feel unwell.

name: Leh
summary: The capital of Ladakh and the base for every ride.
description: Leh is where you acclimatise: an old palace above the bazaar, cafés, Shanti Stupa at sunset and day trips to Thiksey, Hemis and the Indus–Zanskar confluence.

name: Nubra Valley
summary: Sand dunes and double-humped camels beyond Khardung La.
description: Over Khardung La, the Shyok and Nubra rivers meet in a wide valley with white sand dunes at Hunder, the Diskit monastery and orchards in Turtuk near the border.

name: Pangong Lake
summary: A 134 km lake that shifts from turquoise to deep blue.
description: Pangong Tso stretches from Ladakh into Tibet. Camps along the shore make for cold nights and the clearest night sky of the trip.

name: Kashmir
summary: Meadows, houseboats and snow-covered pine forests.
description: From Dal Lake in Srinagar to the meadows of Gulmarg, Sonamarg and Pahalgam, Kashmir is green in summer, golden in autumn and white in winter.
bestSeason: April to October, December to February for snow

name: Srinagar
summary: Houseboats and floating markets on Dal Lake.
description: Stay on a cedar houseboat, take a shikara to the floating vegetable market at dawn and walk the Mughal gardens of Nishat and Shalimar.

name: Gulmarg
summary: One of the highest cable cars in the world.
description: The Gulmarg gondola climbs to Apharwat at almost 4,000 m. In winter it is a ski resort; in summer the meadow is full of wild flowers.
bestSeason: December to March for snow, May to September for meadows

name: Himachal Pradesh
summary: Pine valleys, apple orchards and the road to Spiti.
description: Himachal runs from the colonial hill town of Shimla to the high desert of Spiti. Rivers, cedar forests and some of the most dramatic roads in the country.
bestSeason: March to June, September to November

name: Manali
summary: The starting point of the Manali–Leh highway.
description: Cedar forests along the Beas river, cafés in Old Manali and the Atal Tunnel to Lahaul. Most of our Leh rides start here.
bestSeason: March to June, September to November

name: Spiti Valley
summary: A high-altitude desert with thousand-year-old monasteries.
description: Spiti sits between Tibet and India. Key monastery on its hilltop, the fossil village of Langza, and Chandratal lake at the end of a rough road.

name: Shimla
summary: The old summer capital on a pine ridge.
description: Colonial buildings along the Mall, the toy train from Kalka and forest walks around Jakhoo. The usual first night of a Spiti circuit.
bestSeason: March to June, October to December

name: Uttarakhand
summary: River towns, temple trails and Himalayan sunrises.
description: Uttarakhand has the Ganga at Rishikesh, the hill stations of Mussoorie and Nainital, and views of Nanda Devi and Trishul from Chopta and Auli.

name: Rishikesh
summary: Rafting, yoga and the evening aarti on the Ganga.
description: Suspension bridges over the Ganga, white-water rafting from Shivpuri and the Ganga aarti at Triveni Ghat.

name: Rajasthan
summary: Forts, palaces and nights in the Thar desert.
description: A road trip through Jaipur, Jodhpur and Jaisalmer: hill forts, stepwells, old havelis and a desert camp under the stars.
